entities.summary: Lorraine Althea Constance Monk D.Litt was a Canadian curator, author and executive producer with the National Film Board of Canada who led the production of multiple photography projects chronicling Canadian culture from the 1960s onward. She worked to establish the Canadian Museum of Photography in Toronto, which spawned multiple satellite museums across the country. Over 160,000 of the photographs that she commissioned to detail contemporary Canada are housed at the National Gallery of Canada. She also led the publication of photography books including Canada: A Year of the Land, Call Them Canadians, Canada with Love, Between Friends, and Photographs that Changed the World.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Monk's photography projects chronicled Canadian culture from the 1960s onward, with over 160,000 photographs housed at the National Gallery of Canada. Her work contributed to the establishment of the Canadian Museum of Photography in Toronto.
